prompt: Design a production IaC workflow for network, database and service resources. A recent apply created the network, failed to create the database because of quota, and blocked the service. Two pipelines can currently use the same state; plans are posted as text; the apply identity has administrator access; and a sensitive output was masked in the console but exposed in a plan artifact. Give the immediate recovery and the durable redesign.
directAnswer: Stop concurrent writers and revoke broad artifact access. Preserve the first error, run, exact plan, state lineage/serial, lock and target identity. Determine whether the network remote object exists and whether its binding persisted; do not delete state or blindly rerun. Resolve quota or target error, reconcile ambiguous objects using supported import/state mechanisms, generate and review a new full plan, then verify state, remote and user outcomes. Redesign with protected source, pinned tool/provider/module dependencies, short-lived least-privilege target identity, durable encrypted versioned locked state, separate plan/apply authority, machine-readable exact plan artifacts, policy and human approval bound to a digest, staged apply, secret-safe logs/artifacts, abort and post-change verification.
foundation: IaC applies are partial-capable distributed operations. State is the ownership database, plans are sensitive proposals, and provider credentials are production authority. A safe workflow closes the identity chain from source to target and preserves evidence across failure. Convergence does not replace user, data, security or cost verification.
reasoningSteps: Freeze both pipelines and prevent another writer from changing the same lineage.
Restrict the exposed plan artifact, inspect access logs and rotate any exposed credential or secret.
Preserve source revision, lock, run ID, target principal, tool/provider/module versions, plan digest and first quota error.
Read the latest valid state serial and map the network address to its remote ID.
Inspect the authorized target to determine whether network creation succeeded but state persistence failed or succeeded.
Fix the quota, region or target condition without deleting valid bindings.
Use supported import or state reconciliation only for exact known objects under snapshot and peer review.
Generate a fresh complete plan, review every action and apply only the approved artifact in stages.
Verify provider objects, state serial, network paths, database readiness, service readiness, data/security/cost and user SLI.
Harden the backend with encryption, versioning, locking, audit, tested restore and one writer per state boundary.
Split plan and apply authority, replace administrator access with short-lived least privilege and protect target/network access.
Pin and verify dependencies; validate, test, policy-check and approve the exact plan digest; sanitize and retain artifacts by policy.
seniorAnswer: I would declare the environment partially changed. I would disable both executors, preserve the state serial and lock evidence, restrict the exposed artifact and rotate any real value it contained. Then I would correlate the plan and provider audit with the exact network remote ID. If the network exists and the binding is present, keep it; if it exists without a binding, reconcile through a supported import after proving exclusive ownership; if state persistence is uncertain, restore only from a verified version and compare remote reality. After fixing quota, I would produce a new full plan and apply it through a single controlled writer. The durable workflow would use immutable source and dependency identity, protected locked/versioned state, separate short-lived plan/apply roles, structured plan policy, accountable environment approval, exact-artifact apply, staged blast radius, sensitive artifact controls and multi-dimensional post-checks. A fresh no-change plan closes the model loop; user and data checks close the service loop.
weakAnswer: Force-unlock the state, rerun apply with administrator access and delete the failed resources if the plan still shows changes.
whyWeak: It can race an active writer, destroy valid partial outcomes, repeat ambiguous operations, retain excessive privilege, ignore the secret exposure and create a new plan different from the reviewed proposal.

evidence.signal: Network API reports created and state maps network to net-001
evidence.proves: The selected state and provider observation agree on that binding.
evidence.doesNotProve: Network usability, correct routing or absence of another owner.

evidence.signal: Database failed with quota before returning an object ID
evidence.proves: The recorded call reported that failure path.
evidence.doesNotProve: That no remote object was created unless provider identity/audit confirms it.

evidence.signal: Fresh full plan after recovery has zero changes
evidence.proves: Desired, state and observed provider values converge for that scope.
evidence.doesNotProve: User, data, security, capacity or cost correctness.

evidence.proves: The presentation masked the selected value.
evidence.doesNotProve: Encryption or absence from state, plans, logs and APIs.

followUps.answer: Only after proving the recorded owner is no longer operating, preserving lock/run evidence and obtaining governed approval. It removes serialization, not the underlying failure.

followUps.prompt: Why separate plan and apply roles?
followUps.answer: It reduces the ability of one compromised or mistaken identity to propose, approve and execute a high-risk change and allows plan permissions to be narrower.
Policy efficiently enforces known rules. Humans still judge business intent, data/availability consequence, unknowns and exceptions; both bind to exact inputs.

rubric.observableEvidence: Stops concurrent writers, protects artifacts and preserves first evidence.
Maps exact bindings, handles ambiguity and avoids blind state deletion.
Fixes root condition, creates a new full plan and stages execution.
Pins and verifies tool, provider, module, variables and policy inputs.
Uses locking, encryption, versioning, audit, restore and segmented ownership.
Uses short-lived least privilege, separation of duties and explicit target identity.
Uses machine-readable saved plan, exact digest, rules, exceptions and approval.
Treats plans/state/logs as sensitive, rotates exposure and applies retention/access controls.
Checks state, remote, user, data, security, capacity and cost plus full plan.
States assumptions, owners, abort, rollback/roll-forward, limits and decisions.
